summary: Self-assembled organic monolayers deposited on tantalum and silicon surfaces suppress native oxide regrowth and reduce interfacial two-level-system losses in coplanar waveguide resonators. Internal quality factors reach $1.8 \times 10^6$ at $100$ mK in the single-photon regime, a $\sim140\%$ improvement over untreated devices.
motivation: Tantalum is attractive for superconducting quantum circuits but native oxide formation regenerates after etching, creating high-loss interfacial TLS that degrade coherence times.
method: Self-assembled organic monolayers were deposited on freshly etched tantalum and silicon in CPW resonators; surface films were characterized by contact angle, XPS, FTIR and TEM, and microwave performance measured at $5$–$9$ GHz at $100$ mK.
result: Passivated devices achieved internal quality factors $Q_i = 1.8 \times 10^6$ in the single-photon regime, $\sim140\%$ above control samples with native oxide, with power and temperature dependence confirming reduced TLS-induced dissipation.
